question: Which documents count as Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) for KYC of an individual?
answer_in_own_words: Passport, driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar number, Voter's Identity Card, NREGA job card signed by a State Government officer, and the National Population Register letter containing name and address.

question: What must a Regulated Entity obtain from an individual customer at account opening?
answer_in_own_words: One identity route — Aadhaar number (if receiving subsidies or submitted voluntarily), proof of possession of Aadhaar, any OVD or its equivalent e-document, or a KYC Identifier with consent to fetch records from CKYCR — PLUS the PAN or Form 60, plus any other documents about nature of business/financial status the RE needs.

question: For which customers can an RE use Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP)?
answer_in_own_words: New individual customers; the proprietor in case of proprietorship firms; authorised signatories; and beneficial owners of legal-entity customers.

question: How long must REs preserve transaction records and customer identification records?
answer_in_own_words: Transaction records: at least five years from the DATE OF TRANSACTION. Identification records: at least five years AFTER THE BUSINESS RELATIONSHIP ENDS. (Two different starting points.)

question: How often must periodic KYC updation be done for high, medium and low risk customers?
answer_in_own_words: At least once every 2 years for high-risk, every 8 years for medium-risk, and every 10 years for low-risk customers — counted from account opening or the last KYC updation.

question: What reports must REs furnish to FIU-India, and can they freeze an account just because a report was filed?
answer_in_own_words: REs file Cash Transaction Reports (CTR) and Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) with the Director, FIU-IND, under the PML Rules. They must NOT restrict account operations merely because an STR was filed, and filing must stay confidential.

question: Can I finish opening my bank account over a video call instead of going to the branch?
answer_in_own_words: Yes — through V-CIP: a live, informed-consent audio-visual interaction with an authorised official of the RE, treated on par with face-to-face verification when the prescribed standards are followed.

question: Is my driving licence enough as proof of identity for bank KYC?
answer_in_own_words: Yes — a driving licence is one of the officially recognized identity documents (OVDs) an individual can submit.

question: If I open an account using just an OTP on my Aadhaar-linked phone, are there restrictions on it?
answer_in_own_words: Yes — the account is capped (max ₹1 lakh total balance, ₹2 lakh credited per year, term loans only up to ₹60,000/year), a declaration that you have no other such account is required, and full KYC must be completed within one year or the account stops working.

question: When a company opens a bank account, how does the bank decide who the real owner behind it is?
answer_in_own_words: It must identify the natural person(s) with controlling ownership — more than 10% of shares/capital/profits for a company — or who control it through other means; if no one qualifies, the senior managing official. Companies listed on stock exchanges (and their subsidiaries) are exempt from this identification.

question: Can I give digital copies of my documents from my DigiLocker instead of physical photocopies?
answer_in_own_words: Yes — an 'equivalent e-document' (an electronic document with a valid digital signature, including those issued to a DigiLocker account) is accepted; the RE verifies the digital signature under the IT Act.

question: Do banks apply extra checks when a foreign public official or someone from their family opens an account?
answer_in_own_words: Yes — for such persons (PEPs: people entrusted with prominent public functions BY A FOREIGN COUNTRY), the bank must have systems to identify them, establish their source of funds/wealth, take senior management approval for the account, and monitor it intensively — the same applies to family members and close associates.

question: What are the three monetary limits on accounts opened through Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC?
answer_in_own_words: (1) Aggregate balance across all deposit accounts must not exceed ₹1 lakh; (2) aggregate credits in a financial year must not exceed ₹2 lakh; (3) for borrowing, only term loans, sanctioned amount not exceeding ₹60,000 in a year.

question: What happens if full KYC is not completed within one year for an account opened via OTP-based e-KYC?
answer_in_own_words: Deposit accounts must be closed immediately; for loan (borrowal) accounts, no further debits are allowed. (Also: if the balance crosses ₹1 lakh earlier, the account stops operating until CDD is done.)

question: At what ownership percentage does someone become the beneficial owner of a company, and is the threshold the same for an unincorporated association?
answer_in_own_words: No — for a company (and for a partnership) it is MORE THAN 10% of shares/capital/profits; for an unincorporated association or body of individuals it is MORE THAN 15%. For trusts: author, trustee, and beneficiaries with 10% or more interest.

question: Which circular amended the Master Direction's provision on Aadhaar Face Authentication for e-KYC, and when?
answer_in_own_words: Circular DOR.AML.REC.46/14.01.001/2025-26 dated August 14, 2025 — it amended Explanation 2 of Para 17 (biometric e-KYC including Face Authentication by bank officials/business correspondents).

question: When were the V-CIP provisions substantially amended, and by which circular?
answer_in_own_words: May 10, 2021, vide circular DOR.AML.REC.No.15/14.01.001/2021-22 (it recast both the V-CIP definition and Para 18).

question: What are the four key elements every KYC policy must include?
answer_in_own_words: Customer Acceptance Policy; Risk Management; Customer Identification Procedures (CIP); and Monitoring of Transactions.

question: Can the Principal Officer also be nominated as the Designated Director?
answer_in_own_words: No — in no case shall the Principal Officer be nominated as the Designated Director. (The Designated Director is Board-nominated and both roles' details go to FIU-IND and RBI.)

question: Does a bank need someone to introduce me before I can open an account?
answer_in_own_words: No — REs must ensure that an introduction is NOT sought while opening accounts.

question: At what transaction amount must a walk-in customer be identified by the RE?
answer_in_own_words: When the amount is equal to or exceeds ₹50,000 — as a single transaction or several that appear connected. Identification is also required when someone deliberately structures transactions below the ₹50,000 threshold.

question: Can a bank open an account in an anonymous or benami name?
answer_in_own_words: No — the Customer Acceptance Policy must ensure no account is opened in anonymous or fictitious/benami names.

question: I'm already KYC-verified with my bank — do I have to redo the whole process to open a second account with the same bank?
answer_in_own_words: No — CDD is applied at the UCIC (unique customer identification code) level, so an existing KYC-compliant customer opening another account or taking another product from the SAME RE needs no fresh identification exercise.

question: Will the bank tell me which risk category it has put me in?
answer_in_own_words: No — the risk categorisation and the specific reasons for it are kept confidential from the customer, to avoid tipping off.

question: What must an RE do if it suspects money laundering but fears that doing CDD will tip off the customer?
answer_in_own_words: It shall NOT pursue the CDD process, and instead file an STR with FIU-IND.

question: Can a bank's acceptance policy be used to deny accounts to financially or socially disadvantaged people?
answer_in_own_words: No — the Customer Acceptance Policy must not result in denial of banking to the general public, especially the financially or socially disadvantaged including Persons with Disabilities; no application may be rejected without application of mind, and rejection reasons must be recorded.

question: How often must an RE review its money-laundering and terrorist-financing risk assessment?
answer_in_own_words: At least annually (periodicity set by the Board or its delegated committee; outcome put up to the Board and available to competent authorities).

question: What are the limits on a Small Account?
answer_in_own_words: Aggregate credits in a financial year ≤ ₹1 lakh; aggregate withdrawals and transfers in a month ≤ ₹10,000; balance at any time ≤ ₹50,000 (balance limit not counted for government grants, welfare benefits and procurement payments).

question: I don't have any ID documents at all — can I still open a basic bank account?
answer_in_own_words: Yes — a 'Small Account': the bank takes a self-attested photograph and the customer signs or gives a thumb impression in front of a bank officer. It carries tight transaction limits and works for 12 months, extendable by 12 more if you show you've applied for an OVD.

question: How long does a Small Account stay operational and can that be extended?
answer_in_own_words: Initially 12 months; extendable a further 12 months if the holder furnishes evidence of having applied for an OVD within the first 12 months. Foreign remittances can't be credited unless full KYC is done.

question: If I transfer my account to another branch of the same bank, do I need to redo KYC?
answer_in_own_words: No — KYC done once at one branch/office is valid for transfer to any other branch/office of the same RE, provided full KYC was completed and isn't due for periodic updation.

question: What business proof must a sole proprietorship firm give to open an account, and how many documents?
answer_in_own_words: CDD of the proprietor as an individual, PLUS any TWO documents proving business activity (e.g. Udyam/registration certificate, Shop & Establishment licence, GST certificate, sales/income-tax returns, IEC code, complete ITR, utility bills). At its discretion the RE may accept only ONE, with contact-point verification.

question: Which documents must a company submit to open a bank account?
answer_in_own_words: Certified copies (or equivalent e-documents) of: certificate of incorporation; Memorandum and Articles of Association; the company's PAN; a Board resolution plus power of attorney for those transacting on its behalf; Para-16 documents of those attorney-holders/beneficial owners; names of senior management; and the registered office plus principal place of business if different.

question: Which documents are needed to open an account for a partnership firm?
answer_in_own_words: Registration certificate; partnership deed; the firm's PAN; Para-16 documents of the persons transacting on its behalf; names of ALL partners; and the registered office address plus principal place of business if different.

question: Which documents are needed to open a trust account?
answer_in_own_words: Registration certificate; trust deed; PAN or Form 60 of the trust; Para-16 documents for those transacting on its behalf; names of beneficiaries, trustees, settlor, protector and authors; registered office address; and the list of trustees with documents for those authorised to transact.

question: Where must V-CIP recordings and data be stored?
answer_in_own_words: In systems located in India — stored safely with date-time stamps for easy search; with cloud deployment the data must move to the RE's own/leased servers immediately after the V-CIP and nothing may be retained by the cloud/third-party provider.

question: How recent must an Aadhaar XML file or Aadhaar Secure QR code be when used for V-CIP?
answer_in_own_words: Its generation date must not be older than 3 working days from the date of the V-CIP; more generally the video process must happen within 3 working days of obtaining the identification information if the process can't be completed in one go.

question: What technical safeguards must a bank's V-CIP infrastructure have?
answer_in_own_words: End-to-end encryption between customer device and hosting point; blocking of IP addresses outside India and spoofed IPs; live GPS geo-tagging and date-time stamp on recordings; face liveness/spoof detection and accurate face matching; and Vulnerability Assessment/Penetration Testing/Security Audit by CERT-In empanelled auditors before rollout and periodically.

question: What happens if someone is caught coaching the customer from off-screen during video KYC?
answer_in_own_words: Any prompting observed at the customer's end leads to REJECTION of the account-opening process.

question: When can an account opened through V-CIP start operating?
answer_in_own_words: Only after being subjected to concurrent audit, to ensure the integrity of the process and acceptability of the outcome.

question: Under the 2025 relaxation, until when can a low-risk individual customer with overdue KYC keep transacting?
answer_in_own_words: The RE must allow all transactions and ensure updation within ONE YEAR of KYC falling due or up to JUNE 30, 2026, whichever is later — subject to regular monitoring (introduced by circular DOR.AML.REC.30/14.01.001/2025-26 dated June 12, 2025).

question: How many notices must an RE send a customer about periodic KYC updation?
answer_in_own_words: At least THREE advance intimations (including at least one by letter) before the due date, and at least THREE reminders (including at least one by letter) after the due date — with the system implemented no later than January 1, 2026.

question: Nothing in my KYC details has changed — do I have to visit the branch for periodic updation?
answer_in_own_words: No — a self-declaration of no change is enough, and it can be given through registered email, registered mobile number, ATMs, digital channels (net/mobile banking), or letter.

question: If I declare a new address during KYC updation, what verification happens and how fast?
answer_in_own_words: The declared address must be verified through positive confirmation within TWO MONTHS — by means such as an address verification letter, contact-point verification, or deliverables.
